general.temas: Recurring topics include the death and legacy of Corrado Augias, the war in Ukraine and the meeting between Trump, Xi and Putin. Disagreements within the governing majority also feature, particularly over digital schoolbooks. Only Corriere della Sera highlights the meetings and investigations involving Liguria’s governor, Giovanni Toti.
general.motivo_crispacion: Political tension is reflected in divisions within the governing majority over digital books and, in Corriere, over the Superbonus and the tax on sugary drinks. The strike called by the CGIL adds social protest and harsh language against the budget law. Investigations and allegations linked to Liguria and the alleged courting of Mafia votes heighten tensions, as does the war in Ukraine. Coverage of pensions, savings and culture offers calmer counterpoints.

Corriere della Sera.resumen:
- Several headlines address the contacts Toti and other Ligurian officials had with Spinelli, meetings on his yacht and the alleged manipulation of pandemic data.
- Bucci rejects the allegations related to Spinelli and calls for clarity.
- The reform of the highway code and disagreements within the governing majority over the Superbonus and the drinks tax also feature on the front page.
- The paper reports on the Russian advance towards Kharkiv and the difficult situation acknowledged by Zelensky.
- Other topics include the complaint against Fedez, Camila Giorgi’s tax situation, and investment and savings options.
Corriere della Sera.motivo_populismo: Expressions such as “the case erupts” and criticism of accumulating debt “without thinking about who will pay” add drama and simplification, although facts and quotations predominate and there is no apparent appeal to the people against the elites.
Corriere della Sera.sesgo: The front page focuses on investigations and controversies involving Ligurian officials, with an emphasis on meetings, recordings and alleged irregularities. It also highlights political conflicts and takes a critical stance on debt and the effectiveness of the road traffic reform.

la Repubblica.resumen:
- War reaches Europe’s shores: new attacks on ships and the lack of an effective response from the EU and NATO are denounced.
- The budget law is presented as a response to discontent that fails to address the rising cost of living.
- School reform divides the governing majority; another article examines concentration in the textbook market and the advance of digital technology.
- Several articles remember Corrado Augias, his cultural career and his defence of the right to euthanasia and assisted suicide.
- The paper addresses China’s role as a mediator and Alcaraz’s participation in the Finals despite his physical problems.
la Repubblica.motivo_populismo: Expressions such as “war is already on Europe’s shores” and “the last card” add alarm and drama, although informative headlines predominate and there is no apparent appeal to the people against the elites.
la Repubblica.sesgo: The front page takes a critical approach to the Italian government and to the ability of the EU and NATO to respond. The extensive coverage of Augias is clearly laudatory and highlights his defence of the right to end one’s life.

La Stampa.resumen:
- The government announces a special economic zone for the north, without a tax credit, and the measures involved are explained.
- The general strike on November 20 will mobilise workers and students; the CGIL criticises the budget law.
- Corrado Augias dies at 91 and is remembered for his career in journalism and culture.
- Trump, Putin and Xi meet in Shenzhen: they discuss peace, nuclear risk and the International Criminal Court, with Ukraine as a background issue.
- The front page features curiosities from the summit and examines the case of Jensen Huang in US-China relations.
La Stampa.motivo_populismo: An explanatory tone predominates, although confrontational or emotional expressions such as “The budget stinks” and “attack on the Criminal Court” appear, without a clear appeal to the people against the elites.
La Stampa.sesgo: The front page pays particular attention to the strike and union criticism of the government, alongside practical coverage of its economic measures. It also devotes several sections to the international summit and a laudatory tribute to Augias.

Il Giornale.resumen:
- Trump, Xi and Putin sign a peace declaration centred on the UN and nuclear issues; Meloni attends a summit in Berlin.
- A Pakistani woman reports sexual assaults and violence by relatives in Novellara.
- Corrado Augias dies; the front page highlights his career, his criticism of Meloni and political condolences.
- A headline about the handling of COVID-19 questions Aifa’s rejection of monoclonal antibodies.
- Other topics include the school decree, the Monster of Florence investigation and damage at the University of Turin.
Il Giornale.motivo_populismo: Expressions such as “shock remark”, “four years of venom against Meloni” and “the monster” resort to drama, disparagement and sensationalism, although other headlines maintain an informative tone.
Il Giornale.sesgo: The front page takes a critical approach to Meloni’s detractors, the handling of COVID-19 and university groups, using selection and wording that emphasise conflict and controversy.

Il Fatto Quotidiano.resumen:
- A repentant witness testifies about alleged links between an FdI politician and the Mafia.
- The progressive coalition agrees on a minimum income and criticises the law on antisemitism.
- Opinion articles on fascism and the investigation into the De Gennaro case.
- A motion concerning information about raw-milk cheese in Lombardy is rejected.
- News about entertainment figures, testimony from an athlete who was harassed, and the protection of walruses in Alaska.
Il Fatto Quotidiano.motivo_populismo: Informative or testimonial headlines predominate, but expressions such as “genocide-saving selective anti-racism” and some polemical formulations heighten the emotional and confrontational tone.
Il Fatto Quotidiano.sesgo: The selection and wording show a critical approach to FdI and figures associated with the right, while presenting the minimum income agreement as a measure against poverty. They also include critical opinions on the antisemitism law and the treatment of the memory of fascism.

opiniones.comunista:
Today I see a political debate that talks about businesses while the cost of living is pushed away from the centre of the discussion. The new economic zone for the north promises to make business procedures easier; I would ask what guarantees it offers workers and what resources are being allocated to public services.

The announced general strike is a reminder that wealth is not produced only by those who own capital. I support workers and students organising to demand decent wages, adequate pensions and strong public education and healthcare. The opposition’s agreement on a minimum income is a signal, but fighting poverty also requires changing who makes decisions about the economy. I support forms of collective ownership and democratic control: distributing aid is not enough if the power to determine our living conditions remains concentrated in the hands of big capital.
opiniones.anarquista:
The general strike called in Italy reminds me that working people do not need to wait for parties to give them a voice. When they organise from the bottom up, they can defend their working conditions and build solidarity beyond the ballot box. But unions, too, must be accountable to their members: no hierarchy should speak on behalf of people who have no say.

The opposition’s agreement on a minimum income recognises a real need, although entrusting survival to a measure decided from above leaves dependence on political power intact. I prefer to strengthen mutual aid networks and forms of self-management that allow people to share resources and make decisions collectively, without giving up demands for immediate relief for those who need it. Individual freedom requires material conditions; collective freedom requires that no one monopolise decision-making.
opiniones.liberal:
I am concerned that the budget debate is once again revolving around aid and exemptions while the cost of living bites. I want lower taxes and stable rules, not new taxes on drinks or retroactive changes that penalise decisions made under different conditions. Trust is also an economic resource: without it, investing and hiring become riskier.

The proposal for a minimum income deserves serious consideration, but promising protection is not enough: we need to explain how it will be funded and how it will avoid discouraging work. I prefer a limited safety net that helps those in need without replacing personal responsibility. And I welcome the streamlining of procedures for businesses in the north; it would be better still to extend that freedom to start a business, with less bureaucracy, to everyone.
opiniones.extrema_derecha:
I see an Italy that needs to regain control of its decisions. While the great powers talk of peace, Europe cannot simply wait for others to reach agreements. I want a nation capable of defending its interests and its security, cooperating with its allies without surrendering its sovereignty to them.

At home, the budget debate seems caught up in party disputes while the cost of living weighs on families. I do not believe that accumulating debt or promising universal subsidies can replace a policy that rewards work and protects savings. And the investigations in Liguria demand clarity, without premature convictions: institutions serve citizens, not privileged circles.

I also support a culture that cares for vulnerable people at the end of life. When it comes to euthanasia, I prefer to strengthen support and affirm that no life loses dignity because of illness.
opiniones.centro:
I am concerned that the budget debate is relegating the cost of living to the background. A market economy needs businesses capable of investing, but also a safety net that prevents the most vulnerable families from bearing the cost of crises alone. The progressive agreement on a minimum income deserves serious debate: I would support a financially sustainable benefit, coordinated with employment services and evaluated on its results.

I also believe the strike is an opportunity to listen to workers, not a substitute for negotiation. Government, unions and businesses should seek gradual reforms and verifiable commitments.

In foreign policy, a peace declaration between great powers is not enough if Ukraine is left out. Diplomacy is indispensable, but European security requires respect for the sovereignty of the countries affected and the defence of international institutions.
